root_cause_of_the_false_report: the session miscounted the leading underscores when re-typing the path from a rendered STATE.md view, so it asserted a deleted tree and built the ticket on that. Both `ls` and `rebind-home` had been run against the mis-typed string, so they agreed with each other and both were wrong about the directory.
the_tickets_own_negative_control_is_what: the verify clause asks for rebind-home --auto to converge when saipen_home does NOT resolve, and to converge to no change when it DOES. The antecedent is false here, so the required behaviour is the observed behaviour.

Whether the mirror is meant to lead or follow is a property of the deployment, not something this project's tree can decide, and no gate in this repo reports it.

operator_correction: an earlier report in this session told the operator the SAIPEN home was deleted, that HUNT-001's finding was live because of it, and that T-1394/T-1395 were blocked on a missing engine tree. All three were wrong and are retracted: the home is present, git-backed and remote-configured, so those tickets are ordinary cross-repo engine work, not blocked work.
hunt_001: its reported symptom -- a load_path that does not resolve -- was produced by the same mis-typed path in this session's own shell commands; the launcher itself reported the correct single-underscore path in `continue --json`. HUNT-001 still sits stale-bound for its own recorded reason (source_tree_fingerprint differs) and `sub collect saihunt` still refuses; that part was measured correctly and stands.
